name: Corn (food medium)
description: Food-derived medium: metabolizable components of Corn (Zea mays) [Cereals and cereal products] from FooDB, plus a standard M9 mineral base. Organic components use presence-based uptake bounds; FooDB content retained. Measured compounds with no BiGG exchange are listed under uncovered.

provenance.citation: FooDB v2020-04-07 (Wishart DS et al., foodb.ca). Content sources: DTU, DUKE, PHENOL EXPLORER, Ron G. Buttery and Louisa C. Ling. Volatile Flavor Components of Com Tortillas and Related Products. J. Agrie. Food Chem. 1995, 43, 1878-1882, Ron G. Buttery, Donald J. Stern, and Louisa C. Ling. Studies on Flavor Volatiles of Some Sweet Corn Products. J. Agrie. Food Chem. 1994, 42, 791-795, USDA.
provenance.notes: Organic components mapped from FooDB compounds to BiGG via InChIKey/name. Mineral base added. Bounds presence-based; foodb_content retained. Unmapped measured compounds kept in uncovered (v2 completeness fix). IMPORTANT: composition values are taken from the archived FooDB 2020-04-07 CSV data release; FooDB's live food page no longer displays this bulk composition, so it will appear empty. Verify individual compounds via the per-component cross-reference links. Underlying content was aggregated by FooDB from USDA / DTU / Phenol Explorer.
provenance.verification: expert-curated (multi-source food composition; growth-relevant profile completed, FooDB noise removed)
curation_sources: USDA FoodData Central FDC 169998 (Corn, sweet, yellow, raw; SR Legacy) - full sugar/AA/fatty-acid/vitamin/mineral panel

Ritota et al. / Girolamo 2024, Maize Grain Metabolite Profiling by NMR, Molecules 29(17):4097 doi:10.3390/molecules29174097 (PMC11397060) - grain organic acids citric 16.69, malic 4.91, succinic 2.20 mg/100g dry wt
Peruvian Cabanita maize metabolite study, PMC10011086 - qualitative free-sugar/organic-acid confirmation
provenance.curation_notes: Dominant carbon/energy source is starch (5.7 g/100g in raw sweet corn; up to ~70 g/100g in mature dent grain) plus free glucose 3.43 > fructose 1.94 > sucrose 0.89 g/100g. Organic acids (citric >> malic > succinic) were entirely missing from the FooDB profile and were added; fresh-weight values are transparent conversions of published grain dry-weight NMR means (x0.24 dry-matter) and are order-of-magnitude reliable rather than exact. Profile is for the edible sweet-corn kernel (FDC 169998); matu
curation_added: citric acid (~4.0 mg/100g FW) - dominant kernel organic acid, absent from FooDB
malic acid (~1.2 mg/100g FW) - absent from FooDB
succinic acid (~0.53 mg/100g FW) - absent from FooDB
trans-aconitic acid (qualitative) - characteristic maize organic acid
quantitative free-sugar split (glucose 3.43 > fructose 1.94 > sucrose 0.89 g/100g) with starch 5.70 g/100g
full amino-acid profile with amounts (USDA, incl. corrected L-serine for FooDB 'D-Serine')
lutein + zeaxanthin (644 µg/100g) - dominant corn carotenoids

curation_removed.reason: toxic metalloid soil contaminant, not a nutrient

curation_removed.name: Cholesterol
curation_removed.reason: animal sterol, biologically implausible in a plant kernel; FooDB predicted (maize sterols are beta-sitosterol/campesterol, kept as uncovered)

curation_removed.name: Naphthalene
curation_removed.reason: polycyclic-aromatic environmental contaminant, not a native kernel nutrient

curation_removed.name: 17alpha-ethynylestradiol
curation_removed.reason: synthetic human contraceptive steroid; implausible/predicted, not a food nutrient (in uncovered list)

curation_removed.name: Cyanocobalamin
curation_removed.reason: vitamin B12 does not occur in plant kernels; FooDB artifact (kept in components as 0 for modelling clarity)

coverage_source.definition: pct_covered_all = components / (components + unresolved ingredients) — the legacy metric, which counts pipeline-derived components as covered. pct_covered_source = source-stated components / (those + unresolved ingredients + ingredients replaced by derived components). Component classes come from tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv. A null value means the denominator was zero; it does not mean 100.
